title: Exercise with Social Robots: Companion or Coach?
extended_summary:
This paper asks what role a social robot should play in exercise contexts: a fitness companion that works out alongside the user, or a fitness coach that demonstrates exercises and corrects mistakes. The motivation is to understand how people perceive different robot roles in physical exercise and whether a coach-like role is more acceptable or usable than a companion role.

The study used an online questionnaire built around a pictured and video-described NICO humanoid robot. Participants were shown exercise scenarios and then asked to imagine the robot either as a fitness companion or as a fitness coach. The comparison was not about actual exercise outcomes or behavior change, but about perceptions of the robot artifact, using the Coach-Athlete Relationship Questionnaire, a mind perception scale, and the System Usability Scale.

The sample was very small: 16 respondents completed the questionnaire, and the paper treats the results as preliminary. Across all three measures, the coach condition was rated slightly higher than the companion condition, suggesting that participants found the coach framing more mind-like, more relationship-supportive, and more usable. The authors conclude that the coach persona may be a promising direction for future work, but emphasize that the study is limited by its imagined, non-interactive setup and small sample size.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic social robot / AI-enabled coach concept used to deliver instruction, reminders, demonstrations, and corrective feedback in a physical exercise context.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper compares imagined roles for the NICO social robot as either a fitness companion or a fitness coach; the coach role includes showing exercises to copy and correcting movement mistakes.

findings.finding_summary: This paper does not report academic outcomes or teacher outcomes. It is a pilot questionnaire study in which participants imagined exercising with NICO; the coach condition was rated slightly higher than the companion condition on mind perception, coach-athlete relationship, and usability, but no behavioral change or learning outcome was measured.
findings.measure: Mind perception (agency, experience), CART-Q, System Usability Scale (SUS)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a small questionnaire-based HRI study, not an educational intervention study, and it does not evaluate instructional coaching or teacher planning. The evidence is preliminary and descriptive with no inferential statistics reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported differences are modest and pertain only to participant perceptions of a robot coach versus companion, not to educational or teacher practice outcomes. No effect size is reported, so impact on the requested domains is unclear.
